Leylaz: 'Iran is…
sources: Reuters exclusive by Parisa Hafezi ( ): three senior Iranian officials + one Iranian insider, anonymous; Tehran analyst Saeed Leylaz on the record. Relayed by JPost (by Reuters), Times of Israel, Straits Times, Times
fault_line: Is Tehran's stalling smart leverage — or is it risking the very US/Israeli strike wave it says it's bracing for?

sections.what_happened: Tehran is deliberately prolonging the US-Iran talks to deny Trump a political victory ahead of the Nov 3 midterms; officials say the clerical establishment is 'determined not to give Trump a political victory' and is 'preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal'. Leylaz: 'Iran is influencing the US election without taking any unlawful action.' Reuters adds: 8-month war has driven Trump's approval to a record low; polls show voters worried about high gasoline prices may punish Republicans; Trump says oil prices will drop after the elections but offers no plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz (closed by Iran since Feb, ship traffic 'to a trickle').
sections.what_verified: Six outlets on the same Reuters copy; Leylaz quote identical across all; anonymous officials plausibly senior; directionally consistent with Baqaei's Tuesday presser (US proposal 'insufficient', retaliation doctrine hardened) and the stalled-mediation picture (Axios/Lavrov/Munir threads today).
sections.what_disputed: Anonymous sourcing — officials' stated motive is unverifiable; equally consistent: Tehran stalls because it fears a renewed strike wave and distrusts Washington (the officials themselves say they are convinced Trump is ready to resort to renewed attacks to break the stalemate). US/Israeli position (per Baqaei presser + Trump remarks) is that Tehran refuses concessions on Hormuz/nuclear.
sections.why_matters: Tehran reads Washington's politics better than Washington: the clerical establishment will not hand Trump a pre-midterm win, and the war's price lands on American voters at the pump. Frames with Leylaz's 'influencing the US election without taking any unlawful action' — sharpest quote. Connect to pocketbook angle (gasoline prices, record-low approval).
